A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C2OT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data and image-generation experiments in Tables 1–2, parameter ablations, and generated examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments, revises ImageNet-256 results, and adds original diagnostic, class-conditioned generation, and sensitivity results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the proposed conditional transport formulation remain unchanged, including discrete restrictions, continuous condition weighting, adaptive weight search, and OT oversampling. The additional experiments do not introduce a new generation-method component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds class-conditioned ImageNet-32 generation, whereas v1 evaluates ImageNet-32 with captions. Appendix A.3 adds prediction of conditioning classes from coupled noise across CIFAR resolutions. These extend task coverage within the existing datasets and image domain.

E2.justification: FM and minibatch OT remain the evaluated comparison methods. Table A4 expands OT batch-size settings within the existing comparison, without adding a different comparator. The newly cited Davtyan et al. method is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds distinct diagnostic protocols: path straightness measured with 10,000 samples and 25 integration steps, and condition classification using 100,000 couplings with an 80:20 train/test split. It also adds matched OT/C2OT batch-size evaluations and ground-truth condition-adherence measurements. Existing main-benchmark splits, architectures, and the ImageNet-256 64-epoch budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's batch-size and target-ratio ablations, v3 directly tests path straightness and condition leakage from coupled noise as dimensionality changes. Appendix A also expands batch-size analysis across OT and C2OT, extends target-ratio sensitivity to ImageNet-256, and supplies ground-truth adherence references. These substantially broaden scrutiny of the mechanism and parameter tradeoffs.

E5.justification: For ImageNet-256, v1 reports three seeded evaluations per model, whereas v3 explicitly reports five seeded training runs, both summarized as mean±std. This substantially revises the reported replication unit and uncertainty basis for the principal high-resolution experiment; it is not evidence that v1 had three training runs. Other main-experiment repetition counts are retained.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises the ImageNet-256 results: adaptive FID changes from 7.181 to 5.726 for OT and from 3.290 to 3.369 for C2OT under the revised replication reporting. These are revised estimates, not demonstrated same-protocol performance gains. Tables A1–A6 add diagnostic, class-conditioned ImageNet-32, expanded sensitivity, and reference results. Table 1 and the CIFAR-10 and caption-conditioned ImageNet-32 blocks of Table 2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and prior-skew derivations remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof. Appendix A.1 reproduces a cited path-straightness metric for empirical measurement rather than introducing new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the diagnosis of conditional prior skew, conditional OT weighting, adaptive weight selection, oversampling, and improved conditional-generation performance. The abstract and introduction retain these claims; the shortened conclusion changes emphasis without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly acknowledges weaker benefits on high-dimensional images and hypothesizes that entangled data makes prior skew less harmful. Appendix A.3 relates weaker skew to noisy high-dimensional minibatch OT, while A.5 cautions that the default target ratio is not universally optimal. These qualify the existing interpretation without replacing it.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 identifies the CIFAR adherence classifier as ResNet56 and specifies its repository commit. The retained hyperparameter table, now Table A7, clarifies that its OT batch sizes apply to C2OT. Existing implementation settings and code/data access information otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Davtyan et al., Faster Inference of Flow-Based Generative Models via Improved Data-Noise Coupling, positioning it as concurrent unconditional-coupling research that leaves conditional coupling unresolved. The existing related-work framework and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and typo corrections, adds precise appendix references, shortens the conclusion, and inserts an Additional Experiments appendix before the retained appendices. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Six new appendix tables substantially expand the visual presentation with straightness, class-conditioned generation, condition-prediction, sensitivity, and reference comparisons. Existing figures and generated-image panels are retained; the original hyperparameter Table A1 becomes Table A7. The expansion is chiefly new tabular evidence rather than redesigned figures.

improvement.justification: The added mechanism diagnostics, reported training replication for ImageNet-256, and explicit high-dimensional limitations strengthen the evidence and its interpretation. However, quantitative clarity remains imperfect: Table A1 lists C2OT ImageNet-256 FID 3.70 alongside a 25-step analysis, while Table 2 reports 5.069 at 25 steps, without reconciling the difference. The additions support a limited net improvement despite this reporting issue.
